🎙
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s
remarks to the media
following the 23rd meeting of
the Valdai International Discussion Club
(Moscow Region, September 29, 2026)
❓
Question: German FM Johann Wadephul himself said that he attended
the meeting
solely to avoid being, so to speak, “left out” of the negotiations and leaving the US with a monopoly on the process. So what is Germany seeking – genuine negotiations or some semblance of them? What could move our relations with Berlin forward at this stage?
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
I commented on this in detail at
my news conference in New York
.
It is difficult for me to judge what Germany is seeking.
I think one obvious explanation is simply
a desire
“not to miss the train
”
– the one They believe
“has already picked up speed”
. I do not know whether that is the case. If they mean the Ukrainian crisis, it is difficult for me to judge.
The Ukrainian crisis is intertwined with a vast number of problems across Europe
: the militarisation of the EU, the repeated “mantras” that NATO will expand and admit the Ukrainian regime, that Russia is an eternal enemy, and that
“we will be at war in three years”
.
If these “mantras” are being repeated, and the aim, as Wadephul himself stated, is
simply to repeat them behind closed doors,
without the press
, supposedly to make Russia understand that this is indeed how things stand,
then
this is a futile and, I would even say, harmful exercise
.
It is deeply regrettable
that such figures from the EU and NATO are effectively taking on the role of “spokesmen” for this European scheme.
❓
Question: A few days ago, the Russian Foreign Ministry
announced further contacts with the US
on removing irritants in bilateral relations. Could you tell us whether these contacts have taken place, which specific irritants are currently on the agenda and, in particular, whether there are realistic prospects for the return of diplomatic property?
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
The contacts have not yet taken place.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and I agreed that they would take place soon
. Our experts need to agree on the specific dates and venue.
The discussions will focus on
the functioning of our respective diplomatic missions
– Russia’s in the US and America’s in Russia. There are many issues, including, of course,
diplomatic property
.
We have heard
no encouraging comments on this issue
from the Americans under the Donald Trump administration.
❓
Question: You said that reality would compel the US to think
in terms of multilateralism
. Yet, for now, we see key players in Eurasia and the Middle East – the US, Iran, Israel and the Gulf monarchies – stuck in a zero-sum mindset. Do you see any prospects at all for creating a new security system in these regions? Is Russia prepared to act as a guarantor of a balance of interests if everyone else continues to pursue an “all-or-nothing” approach?
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
I said that
reality
would compel them.
But life is only just beginning. Be patient.
President Putin and I have repeatedly set out all
our proposals
on how to build relations in the international arena
. We stand for honest dialogue on an equal footing and for taking each other’s interests into account.
What we are seeing in US policy today is, of course,
an effort to advance its own interests unilaterally.
However, the US has to engage with countries such as
Russia
and
China
. These contacts involve discussions of steps that would serve the interests of both sides.
👉
That is precisely what I meant when I said that “reality would compel them”
.
❓
Question: Poland plans to manufacture Patriot missiles on its territory. At what point would European countries’ involvement in the Ukrainian conflict require Russia to respond with direct military action?
💬
Sergey Lavrov:
We have
our military doctrine
that addresses this, which President Vladimir Putin has cited
on numerous occasions
.
☝️
I urge you to study the relevant sections of this fundamental document carefully.
Read in full

⚡️
Comment by the Russian Embassy in Belgium on the escalation of the military-political situation around the Kaliningrad Region by NATO countries
(September 28, 2026)
We are deeply concerned by the provocative statements and actions of the North Atlantic Alliance's leadership and NATO member states with respect to the Kaliningrad Region, an integral part of the Russian Federation.
We observe an
unprecedented surge in the Alliance's military activity along our western borders
. Initiatives aimed at containing the alleged “Russian threat” are expanding, with large-scale exercises rehearsing offensive operations.
In the Baltic region, the Alliance is constantly seeking to create new threats to our fleet, openly modeling specific scenarios for detaching the Kaliningrad Region and developing plans for the military and political isolation of the northwestern ports.
In January 2025, Operation "Baltic Sentry" was launched, aimed at testing mechanisms for the unilateral blocking of international shipping.
Simultaneously we are witnessing a
sharp escalation in the rhetoric of Western military and political circles, particularly on the eastern flank
. Deliberately raising the level of confrontation, they are making statements claiming that NATO has the capability to strike military targets in the Kaliningrad region and calling for new "aggressive" exercises to be organised near Russia’s borders.
The Alliance is conducting a large-scale information campaign to propagate the myth of the ‘Russian threat’ and to spread false information about Moscow’s alleged "intentions’ to attack one of the Baltic states by 2029 at the latest, or even sooner. Plans are being announced for the cross-border evacuation of the population"in the event of a major crisis".
At the same time,
the statements repeatedly made by our country’s highest leadership - that it has no intentions or motives to initiate any military action - as well as the proposal to NATO countries to set out mutual security guarantees in writing, are being completely ignored.
❗️
In light of the aggressive stance pursued by the bloc’s leadership and member states,
the Embassy has conveyed our fundamental positions to the NATO International Staff and the Belgian Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
We have warned that the aforementioned reckless and irresponsible course of action sharply increases the risks of a direct armed conflict with our country. We have emphasised that Russia possesses the necessary means to repel any potential aggression and is prepared to deploy its entire arsenal to defend its territory should NATO countries attempt to isolate the Kaliningrad region from the rest of our country.
We have called on the bloc’s member states to refrain from further escalatory statements and actions in order to prevent a large-scale confrontation.

***
In April 2023 Kiev began circulating
the myth of “20,000 abducted Ukrainian children”.
It was first promoted by Ukraine's Commissioner for Children’s Rights Daria Gerasimchuk and quickly amplified by Western mainstream media.
The “19,546 deported kids” figure
published by the Children of War portal was not backed by any lists, names or individual records.
The Russian side
received an actual list
of “abducted Ukrainian children” only in 2025 during resumed Russia-Ukraine direct talks in Istanbul. It contained
only 339 names
, showing that the number of children separated from their families on both sides had been grossly inflated for political PR.
A case-by-case review showed that a large share of those listed as “children” were actually adults who
had already turned 18
when the special military operation started. Some were found legally residing in Russia with one of the parents, while
over 100 were found in Germany
– a revelation Ukraine quickly tried to hide.
Meanwhile, Russia has maintained
a clear and transparent family-reunification process
, coordinated by
the Office of the Presidential Commissioner for Children’s Rights
. Since 2022,
145 children from 118 families
have been reunited with parents or close relatives in Ukraine or third countries.
32 children
from 24 families
have returned to Russia from Ukraine. All reunifications are verified and accompanied by
the International Committee of the Red Cross
.
‼️
The Russian side remains open to constructive dialogue.
We highly appreciate the mediation efforts of the International Committee of the Red Cross, the Vatican and Qatar
, which also provides substantial logistical assistance.
Since autumn 2025, First Lady of the United States
Melania Trump
has joined these important efforts
.

#NoStatuteOfLimitations
🕯
September 29 marks the 85th anniversary of the beginning of
the mass shooting of the Jewish population
by the Nazis at
the Babi Yar ravine
on the outskirts of occupied Kiev.
On September 29–30, 1941, the Nazis and their collaborators rounded up Kiev’s Jews and forced them to Babi Yar. Many had no inkling until the very last moment that death awaited them. Others, realising what was happening, embraced, said their goodbyes, and prayed.
In the space of two days,
33,771 people were shot
– predominantly women, children, and the elderly. People were driven into the ravine and gunned down with machine-gun fire. The sound of the shots was drowned out by music and the noise of a plane flying overhead.
💬
Mikhail Sidko, who was six years old at the time of the tragedy – one of the few survivors of Babi Yar – recalled:
Many lost their senses right there, realising what was about to happen to them. They screamed, were shot, and then dragged by their legs into the ravine.
Mass executions at Babi Yar continued right up until Kiev was liberated by the Red Army. In total, between 1941 and 1943,
over 120,000 people of various ethnic backgrounds were killed there
– Jews, Roma, Poles – as well as Soviet prisoners of war and camp inmates, clergy, underground resistance members, and others.
Sonderkommando 4a, part of Einsatzgruppe C,
bore direct responsibility for the mass killings.
Ukrainian nationalists serving in the auxiliary police also took an active part in the atrocities.
As they retreated from Kiev, the Nazis attempted to destroy the evidence of their crimes by exhuming and burning tens of thousands of bodies. Nevertheless, they failed to conceal the scale of the atrocities committed. The few survivors of Babi Yar later testified at the Nuremberg Trials. Paul Blobel, who oversaw the exhumation and the destruction of evidence regarding the mass killings, was sentenced to death and hanged.
▪️
Babi Yar became
one of the most notorious sites
of the mass extermination of Jews during the Holocaust – a grim symbol of Nazi terror and crimes against the civilian population.
The mass extermination of people at Babi Yar marks one of the most tragic chapters of World War II. Remembering these crimes is our shared duty and serves as a reminder that any manifestation of neo-Nazism is unacceptable.
☝️
Starting this year, Russia observes
April 19
as
the Day of Remembrance for the Victims of the Genocide of the Soviet People
Committed by the Nazis and Their Accomplices during the Great Patriotic War.
❗️
Russian diplomacy will continue to seek international recognition of the crimes committed by the Nazis and their accomplices against citizens of the Soviet Union, including the mass killings at Babi Yar, as acts of genocide against the Soviet people.
#WeRemember

item.title: ⚛️ Happy Nuclear Industry Workers’ Day! September 28 is a day dedicated in Russia to people whose work requires not only profound knowledge and the highest level of responsibility,
item.description: ⚛️ Happy Nuclear Industry Workers’ Day! 🇷🇺 September 28 is a day dedicated in Russia to people whose work requires not only profound knowledge and the highest level of responsibility, but also genuine dedication to their profession. The nuclear industry is not only about reactors, technologies and highly sophisticated scientific research. Above all, it is about people - scientists, engineers, designers, power engineers, construction specialists, radiation safety professionals, doctors, educators, diplomats and thousands of other dedicated professionals whose daily work advances science, energy and industry. Behind every new project, scientific breakthrough and technological achievement stand years of hard work, the experience of several generations and a responsibility towards the future . Special words of gratitude go to the veterans of the nuclear industry , who laid the foundations for its development, and to the young professionals who will carry this work forward and create the technologies of tomorrow. We wish everyone who has devoted their lives to the nuclear industry good health, well-being, professional success and new achievements! May the power of the atom always serve peace, progress and development . 🤝 Happy Nuclear Industry Workers’ Day!

, who laid the foundations for its development, and to the young professionals who will carry this work forward and create the technologies of tomorrow.
We wish everyone who has devoted their lives to the nuclear industry
good health, well-being, professional success and new achievements!
May the power of the atom
always serve peace, progress and development
.
🤝
Happy Nuclear Industry Workers’ Day!

🗓
On September 26,
the 12th St Petersburg International United Cultures Forum
concluded at
the State Hermitage Museum
. The Forum became
a major event dedicated to promoting intercultural dialogue
and strengthening understanding between countries and peoples, while preserving their linguistic, cultural and spiritual identities.
The Forum
brought together
4,500 participants
, including
45 official delegations
, with
representatives from
73 countries
. Delegations from
more than 10 countries
were led by their Ministers of Culture.
💬
The Forum’s central event was
an address
by President of Russia
Vladimir Putin
:
Culture can build bridges between people
. It is a vital and irreplaceable means of communication and dialogue where political and economic ties have been frozen or brought to a halt by disagreements, sanctions and restrictions.
Russia has historically developed as a crossroads of peoples, languages and traditions
. For us, unity means solidarity built on nurturing the distinct identity and development of every people and ethnic group.
Culture plays a key role in this process
, just as it does in our complex world, with its conflicts, profound technological and social transformations, and competition between countries.
👉
Read the full transcript of President Putin’s address to the Forum
The Forum featured
84 events
across ten thematic tracks
, covering museums, theatre, music, film, cultural sovereignty, education, artificial intelligence and other subjects.
✍️
Participants signed 33 agreements
to develop cooperation in culture, museums, theatre, education and the preservation of cultural heritage.
Plans were set in motion to develop a
concept for theatre development through 2035
and expand cooperation with professional associations in
Vietnam, Arab countries and Iran
. Russia also signed a number of bilateral documents with friendly countries.
💬
Russia’s Minister of Culture
Olga Lyubimova
:
Once again, our Forum has confirmed its standing as
a respected platform for open and free dialogue
, bringing together representatives of different countries, peoples and cultures around a common goal: identifying the challenges facing world culture and finding ways to address them.
#UnitedCulturesForum
